newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X sets new lows in Toronto gray market trading.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X sets new lows in Toronto gray market trading.

text.p: Trading in shares of disgraced Bre-X Minerals Ltd resurfaced at new lows in the gray market on Monday in selling to retail investors by small brokerages after being delisted from most stock exchanges.
Bre-X, once worth C$28.65 a share after a 10-for-one stock split, were trading in a range of C$0.01 to C$0.03 each, fuelled mainly by demand from souvenir hunters, traders said.

Calgary-based Bre-X, once in control of what was touted as the world's largest gold deposit in Indonesia, saw its find exposed as a fraud on May 4. Shares were stripped of their trading status on the Toronto, Nasdaq and Alberta stock markets and suspended on the Montreal exchange.
The company's stock is posted on the Canadian Dealing Network under the symbol BXMN, but no trades had been registered by mid-afternoon.
"The only people I've seen who want to buy it want a certificate for their wall," one equities trader said.
Another said some investors were willing to take a risk on the stock because they believed the deposit might still turn out to be worth something.
At 219 million shares, Bre-X has a market capitalization of some C$2.2 to C$6.6 million, against a peak of over C$6.0 billion (US$4.4 billion).
